# `radio`

Group: **Radio**. The radio stack: which technology, at which fidelity, with which models.

98 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see [how to read these tables](../overview.md). Paths use `[]` for a list element and `*` for a map key.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } | `wired` |
| :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } | `partial` |

## phy

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-radio-phy-data-rate-mbps"></span>`radio.phy.data_rate_mbps` | number | Mbit/s | | [3, 27]<br>recommended 6 Mbit/s (the US default); 3 for range, 12 to 18 for crowded channels. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The data rate every safety frame is sent at, Mbit/s: one of 3, 4.5, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24 or 27 (the eight 10 MHz OFDM rates of IEEE 802.11-2020 Table 17-4). A higher rate takes less air time per frame but needs a stronger signal, so it trades range for channel capacity. Unset is 6 Mbit/s, the SAE J2945/1 default. The 802.11p data rate (modulation and coding). Faster rates finish each frame sooner, so more radios fit on the channel, but they need a stronger signal, so range shrinks. |
| <span id="s-radio-phy-noise-figure-db"></span>`radio.phy.noise_figure_db` | number | dB | | [0, 15]<br>recommended 6 dB (automotive module) to 9 dB (3GPP UE). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The receiver noise figure, dB: how much noise the receiver's own electronics add on top of the thermal floor of −104 dBm in 10 MHz. Unset is the hardware figure the PHY card cites (6 dB). How much noise the receiver's own electronics add; every extra dB costs about 10 % of range in free space. |
| <span id="s-radio-phy-sensitivity-dbm"></span>`radio.phy.sensitivity_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-105, -60]<br>recommended -92 dBm (fielded units) to -85 dBm (ETSI minimum). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | One receiver sensitivity at every data rate, dBm: a frame weaker than this is not decoded (Veins' `minPowerLevel`). Unset uses the per-rate table that `radio.models.phy` selects (fielded units, −92 dBm at 6 Mbit/s). The weakest frame the receiver decodes, at every data rate (Veins' minPowerLevel). |
| <span id="s-radio-phy-cca-threshold-dbm"></span>`radio.phy.cca_threshold_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-100, -50]<br>recommended -85 dBm (ETSI); -82 (ns-3); -65 (Veins). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The carrier-sense (CCA) threshold, dBm: energy above it makes a radio treat the channel as busy, defer its transmission and count the time in the channel busy ratio. Unset is −85 dBm (ETSI EN 302 571 §4.2.10.1). The signal level at which a radio hears the channel as busy and holds back; it also sets what the channel busy ratio counts. |
| <span id="s-radio-phy-energy-detect-dbm"></span>`radio.phy.energy_detect_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-100, -50]<br>recommended -65 dBm (IEEE 802.11-2020 §17.3.10.6, 10 MHz); -62 (ns-3); -85 reproduces the older single-threshold carrier sense. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The energy-detect level, dBm: another channel's frame leaking through the channel filter holds carrier sense busy only above it (and, under SAE J2945/1, counts in the CBP only above it). Unset is −65 dBm, 20 dB above the 10 MHz minimum sensitivity (IEEE 802.11-2020 §17.3.10.6); never below `cca_threshold_dbm`. −85 dBm holds a leak to the preamble level. The level at which another channel's frame, leaking through the filter, makes the radio hear its own channel as busy. |
| <span id="s-radio-phy-capture-threshold-db"></span>`radio.phy.capture_threshold_db` | number | dB | | [0, 30]<br>recommended Unset (error model); 4 to 10 dB to compare with threshold-based simulators. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A hard capture threshold, dB: a frame is decoded only while it stays this far above the interference plus noise (Torrent-Moreno 2009, Eq. 1). Unset uses the SINR trace against the error model, as Veins does. Replaces the error model with a hard rule: a frame survives only if it stays this many dB above interference plus noise. |

## mac

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-radio-mac-edca-profile"></span>`radio.mac.edca_profile` | string | | `by-region` | `by-region`, `sae-j2945-1`, `en-302-663`<br>recommended By region (the default); SAE J2945/1 or EN 302 663 to compare the two on one map. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Which EDCA table the MAC contends with, and so where a BSM waits (`EdcaProfileSpec`). Unset is `by-region`: SAE J2945/1 Table 18 for 802.11p under a US region, ETSI EN 302 663 elsewhere (`wiring::edca_profile`). An explicit `cw_min_*` or `aifsn_*` below still wins over the table's own value. Which table of waiting times the radio uses before it sends: the US safety-message standard's, where a routine safety message waits a little longer than an emergency one, or the European default. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-periodic-access-category"></span>`radio.mac.periodic_access_category` | string | | | `vo`, `vi`, `be`, `bk`<br>recommended Video for a US BSM (SAE J2945/1 user priority 5) or a European CAM; voice is a critical BSM's. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The access category periodic awareness messages (BSM, CAM, PSM, VAM, CPM, SPaT, MAP) are queued in: `vo`, `vi`, `be` or `bk`. Unset is `vo`, the highest, except for a BSM under SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (below). SAE J2945/1 §6.3.4 puts a BSM without a critical event flag at user priority 5, which is AC_VI (`UPEDCA-001`), and one with a flag at user priority 7, AC_VO (`UPEDCA-002`); EN 302 663 Annex C puts the CAM at `vi`. Unset under SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (`MacSettings::edca_profile`), a BSM is queued by its flags in exactly that way (`wiring::bsm_queue_by_flags`); set, it names the queue of every periodic message, the BSM included. The priority queue awareness messages wait in; higher priorities wait less before sending. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-event-access-category"></span>`radio.mac.event_access_category` | string | | | `vo`, `vi`, `be`, `bk`<br>recommended Voice. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The access category event messages (DENM, forwarded hazard warnings) are queued in. Unset is `vo` (EN 302 663 Annex C). The priority queue hazard warnings (DENM) wait in. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-cw-min-vo"></span>`radio.mac.cw_min_vo` | integer | slots | | [1, 1023]<br>recommended 3 (standard) to 15 in dense traffic. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `CWmin` of the voice category, slots: a frame waits a random 0 to `CWmin` idle slots before it may start. A larger window means fewer collisions and more delay. Unset is 3 (EN 302 663 Table C.4). Broadcast never doubles it, so there is no `CWmax` to set. The random back-off window of the voice queue: a wider window spreads transmissions out, which means fewer collisions and more delay. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-aifsn-vo"></span>`radio.mac.aifsn_vo` | integer | slots | | [2, 15]<br>recommended 2 (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `AIFSN` of the voice category, slots: the fixed idle wait before the countdown. Unset is 2. The fixed idle wait of the voice queue before its back-off countdown. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-cw-min-vi"></span>`radio.mac.cw_min_vi` | integer | slots | | [1, 1023]<br>recommended 15 under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18), 7 elsewhere (EN 302 663). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `CWmin` of the video category, slots. Unset is 15 for 802.11p under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18) and 7 elsewhere (EN 302 663). The random back-off window of the video queue. |
| <span id="s-radio-mac-aifsn-vi"></span>`radio.mac.aifsn_vi` | integer | slots | | [2, 15]<br>recommended 4 under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18), 3 elsewhere (EN 302 663). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `AIFSN` of the video category, slots. Unset is 4 for 802.11p under a US region (SAE J2945/1 Table 18) and 3 elsewhere (EN 302 663). The fixed idle wait of the video queue. |

Unset is 64. How many frames wait in each priority queue before new ones are dropped. |

## channel_model

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-path-loss-exponent"></span>`radio.channel_model.path_loss_exponent` | number | | | [1.5, 6]<br>recommended 1.8 (highway) to 3.5 (dense city). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A single-slope path-loss exponent: 2 is free space, about 2.7 to 3.5 a city street. Setting it, or the shadowing spread, runs the log-distance law (`propagation/log-distance-shadowing`) with these numbers over a free-space anchor at 10 m. Unset keeps the measured dual-slope fits. How fast the signal weakens with distance: 2 in free space, near 3 in a built-up street. Setting it runs the log-distance law. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-shadowing-sigma-db"></span>`radio.channel_model.shadowing_sigma_db` | number | dB | | [0, 15]<br>recommended 3 to 4 dB in line of sight, 6 to 7 dB obstructed. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The log-normal shadowing standard deviation, dB: how much the received power wanders around the path-loss mean as buildings and trucks come and go. Unset keeps the fit's own (about 4 dB in line of sight, 6 to 7 dB obstructed, Abbas 2015). How much the signal wanders around its average as buildings and trucks block it. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-shadowing-decorrelation-m"></span>`radio.channel_model.shadowing_decorrelation_m` | number | m | | (0, 500]<br>recommended 10 m (city) to 50 m (highway). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How far a vehicle moves before its shadowing is uncorrelated with what it was, metres (Gudmundson 1991). Unset is the environment's (about 10 m in a city). How far a vehicle travels before its shadowing changes completely. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-fading"></span>`radio.channel_model.fading` | string | | | `none`, `rayleigh`, `rice`, `nakagami`<br>recommended Leave unset (Nakagami m = 3); Rayleigh for a worst case. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The small-scale fading law: `none`, `rayleigh` (no direct path), `rice` (a direct path `rice_k_db` stronger than the scatter) or `nakagami` (shape `nakagami_shape`). Unset keeps the tier's choice (Nakagami m = 3 for 802.11p). The fast signal fluctuation as vehicles move a few centimetres: Rayleigh has no direct path, Rice and Nakagami have one. It is the main cause of losses well inside range. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-fading-coherence"></span>`radio.channel_model.fading_coherence` | string | | | `independent`, `doppler`<br>recommended independent (today's behaviour); doppler for burst-loss studies (Akki &amp; Haber 1986; Rappaport 2002 Eq. 5.40c). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How the fade of one link changes from frame to frame: `independent` (each frame draws its own, the default) or `doppler` (one fade per coherence time, `0.423 / f_D` with `f_D` from both ends' speeds and the carrier, so slow links fade in bursts and fast links decorrelate; Akki &amp; Haber 1986, Rappaport 2002 Eq. 5.40c). Whether a link's fade carries over from one message to the next: with doppler, vehicles standing still (a queue at a red light) keep a bad fade for many messages in a row, while fast vehicles get a fresh fade with every message. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-nakagami-shape"></span>`radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape` | number | | | [0.5, 20]<br>recommended 1 to 5. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The Nakagami shape `m` when `fading` is `nakagami` (written `m` in the literature): 1 is Rayleigh, larger is milder. Unset is 3. The Nakagami shape m: 1 is Rayleigh, larger values are milder fading. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-rice-k-db"></span>`radio.channel_model.rice_k_db` | number | dB | | [-10, 30]<br>recommended 3 to 10 dB. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The Rice factor `K` when `fading` is `rice`, dB: the direct path's power over the scattered power's. Unset is 6 dB. The strength of the direct path over the scattered ones in a Rice channel. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-nakagami-shape-far"></span>`radio.channel_model.nakagami_shape_far` | number | | | [0.5, 20]<br>recommended 0.75 to 1 beyond about 80-100 m. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The Nakagami `m` beyond `nakagami_breakpoint_m`, when `fading` is `nakagami`, for a channel that gets harsher with range (Veins-style: about 1.5 near, 0.75 far). Needs the breakpoint. Unset keeps `nakagami_shape` at every distance. The fading severity beyond the breakpoint distance, for a channel that gets harsher with range. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-nakagami-breakpoint-m"></span>`radio.channel_model.nakagami_breakpoint_m` | number | m | | (0, 5000]<br>recommended 80 to 100 m. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The distance at which the Nakagami `m` switches to `nakagami_shape_far`, metres. The distance at which the fading switches to its far-away severity. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-building-wall-loss-db"></span>`radio.channel_model.building_wall_loss_db` | number | dB | | [0, 40]<br>recommended 9 dB (Sommer 2011 default); 2.4 dB for light construction. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How much each building wall the signal passes through costs (Sommer 2011 β), dB: 9 dB for the fitted default, about 2.4 dB for light construction. How much each building wall between two cars costs the signal (Sommer 2011's β, as Veins models it). |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-building-loss-db-per-m"></span>`radio.channel_model.building_loss_db_per_m` | number | dB/m | | [0, 10]<br>recommended 0.4 dB/m (Sommer 2011 default); 0.1-0.63 dB/m across the fitted rows. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How much each metre of path inside a building costs (Sommer 2011 γ), dB per metre: 0.4 for the fitted default. How much each metre of the path inside a building costs (Sommer 2011's γ). |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-vehicle-blockage"></span>`radio.channel_model.vehicle_blockage` | boolean | | | recommended On for realism; off to measure what blockage costs. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether other vehicles between two antennas attenuate the signal (3GPP TR 37.885 NLOSv blockage). On by default with the city-street law; off makes vehicles radio-transparent, on charges them under every law. Whether trucks and cars between two antennas weaken the signal (3GPP TR 37.885 NLOSv). |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-foliage"></span>`radio.channel_model.foliage` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on with world.vegetation for suburban and rural maps with woods and tree-lined streets. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether a path through trees loses the foliage excess (ITU-R P.833 §3.1 with GEMV²'s 2.3 dB/m at 5.9 GHz, capped at the diffraction over the canopy: `obstacle/foliage/p833`). Needs `world.vegetation`. Unset is off. Whether trees between two antennas weaken the signal: about 2.3 dB per metre of trees at 5.9 GHz, up to what bending over the treetops would cost. Needs world.vegetation. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-density-sigma"></span>`radio.channel_model.density_sigma` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today, a fixed spread); on for the measured dependence on surroundings. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether the log-distance law's shadowing σ grows with the vehicles and buildings around the link (GEMV², Boban et al. 2014 eq. 10: 3.3 dB on an empty road to 5.2 dB downtown for line of sight). Unset keeps the preset's fixed σ. Whether the signal's random variation grows with the traffic and buildings around each link, as measured in Porto (GEMV2): calmer on an empty road, rougher downtown. |
| <span id="s-radio-channel-model-reflection"></span>`radio.channel_model.reflection` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today); on for downtown maps, where reflections carry links round corners. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether a building-blocked link also receives the strongest single specular reflection off a building wall, power-summed with the shadowed path (GEMV², Boban et al. 2014 §IV-B.3, eqs. 6-8; ITU-R P.2040-3 Table 3 for the walls: `obstacle/reflection/gemv2-single-bounce`). Needs buildings. Unset is off. Whether a signal blocked by a building can still arrive by bouncing once off another building's wall, as it does down a street canyon: the bounce costs its longer path and the wall's reflection loss. |

## dcc

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-enabled"></span>`radio.dcc.enabled` | boolean | | | recommended On, except as the baseline of a congestion study. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether 802.11p congestion control runs at all. `false` lets every radio send at its full rate and power however busy the channel is: the baseline a DCC study compares against. Unset is on (EN 302 571 requires it in Europe). Congestion control: radios slow down or turn their power down when the channel is busy, so the channel stays usable. Turn it off to measure what it buys. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-cbr-target"></span>`radio.dcc.cbr_target` | number | | | [0.1, 0.95]<br>recommended 0.6 to 0.7 (standard 0.68). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The channel load the ETSI adaptive algorithm steers towards, as a fraction of time busy. Unset is 0.68 (TS 102 687 V1.2.1 Table 3). The share of time busy the ETSI adaptive algorithm aims the channel at. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-adaptive-alpha"></span>`radio.dcc.adaptive_alpha` | number | | | [0.001, 0.5]<br>recommended 0.016 (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The ETSI adaptive smoothing factor α: how much of each new load measurement enters the running average. Unset is 0.016 (ibid.). How quickly the ETSI adaptive algorithm's load average follows new measurements. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-adaptive-beta"></span>`radio.dcc.adaptive_beta` | number | | | [0.0001, 0.05]<br>recommended 0.0012 (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The ETSI adaptive gain β: how hard the allowed duty cycle reacts to the gap from the target. Unset is 0.0012 (ibid.). How strongly the ETSI adaptive algorithm changes the allowed airtime when the load is off target. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-max-itt-ms"></span>`radio.dcc.max_itt_ms` | number | ms | | [100, 2000]<br>recommended 600 ms (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The longest interval SAE J2945/1 may stretch a BSM's spacing to under congestion, ms (`vMax_ITT`). Unset is 600 ms. The longest gap J2945/1 allows between one vehicle's BSMs under congestion. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-density-coefficient"></span>`radio.dcc.density_coefficient` | number | vehicles | | [1, 200]<br>recommended 25 (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The vehicle density at which SAE J2945/1 starts to stretch the interval (`B`, vehicles within 100 m). Unset is 25. How many neighbours within 100 m J2945/1 tolerates before it stretches the BSM interval. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-power-control"></span>`radio.dcc.power_control` | boolean | | | recommended On (J2945/1); off for rate-only control. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether SAE J2945/1 also lowers the radiated power as the channel fills. Unset is on (J2945/1 §6.3.8); J3161/1 for LTE-V2X has none. Whether J2945/1 also turns the radiated power down as the channel fills. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-min-power-dbm"></span>`radio.dcc.min_power_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-10, 20]<br>recommended 10 dBm (standard). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The lowest power J2945/1's power control may go to, dBm (`vRP_Min`). Unset is 10. The lowest power J2945/1's power control may reach. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-reactive-table"></span>`radio.dcc.reactive_table` | string | | | `a1`, `a2`<br>recommended A.1 for secured CAMs at 6 Mbit/s; A.2 only for short frames. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | ETSI reactive DCC's table (TS 102 687 V1.2.1 Annex A): `a1` (frames up to 1 ms on air, Table A.1, the default) or `a2` (up to 500 µs, Table A.2, twice the rates). Which ETSI reactive table sets the message rate in each congestion state: A.1 for frames up to 1 ms on air, A.2 (twice the rates) for frames up to 500 µs. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-reactive-hold-ms"></span>`radio.dcc.reactive_hold_ms` | number | ms | | [0, 5000]<br>recommended 0 (the tables give none) to 1,000 ms. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | ETSI reactive DCC's state-hold time, ms: how long a state is held before the next step. 0 unless set (the tables specify no hysteresis). How long reactive congestion control stays in a state before it may step again; longer holds damp oscillation. |
| <span id="s-radio-dcc-channel-quality"></span>`radio.dcc.channel_quality` | string | | | `sae-j2945-1`, `fmvss150-nprm`<br>recommended SAE J2945/1 Eq. 4 (the default); the FMVSS 150 NPRM smoothing only to reproduce older results. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | SAE J2945/1's channel-quality indicator Π: `sae-j2945-1` (unset) is 6.3.8.1 Eq. 4, the mean PER of the neighbours within 100 m capped at 0.3; `fmvss150-nprm` smooths it with weight 0.9 on the previous value, as the withdrawn FMVSS 150 NPRM transcribed it. How SAE J2945/1 judges the channel from its neighbours' lost messages, which decides how often it assumes they missed its last BSM and sends an extra one. |

## sidelink

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-reservation-interval-ms"></span>`radio.sidelink.reservation_interval_ms` | integer | ms | | [1, 1000]<br>recommended 100 ms for 10 Hz BSMs; 20 or 50 ms for faster traffic. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How often a radio's reserved resource repeats, ms (the resource reservation interval, RRI). LTE allows 20, 50, 100 or a multiple of 100 up to 1,000 (TS 36.331 `sl-ResourceReservationPeriod`); NR also 1 to 99. Unset is 100 ms, one BSM period. How often a C-V2X radio's booked slot repeats; it should match how often the radio has a message to send. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-resource-keep-probability"></span>`radio.sidelink.resource_keep_probability` | number | | | [0, 0.8]<br>recommended 0.8 (J3161/1); 0 to study fast reselection. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The probability a radio keeps its resource when the reselection counter runs out (`probResourceKeep`): 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 or 0.8 (TS 36.331). Higher keeps reservations stable for others to sense, but makes two radios that collide keep colliding. Unset is the profile's (0.8 under SAE J3161/1). The chance a radio keeps its booked slot when its counter runs out, rather than picking a new one. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-rsrp-threshold-dbm"></span>`radio.sidelink.rsrp_threshold_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-128, -60]<br>recommended -128 dBm (NR studies) to -110 dBm (LTE studies). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The RSRP above which a resource another radio reserved is excluded from selection, dBm; it is raised 3 dB at a time until enough candidates remain (TS 36.213 §14.1.1.6). Unset is the profile's (−128 dBm NR, −110 dBm LTE studies). How strong another radio's booking must be for a radio to avoid that slot. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-sensing"></span>`radio.sidelink.sensing` | boolean | | | recommended On; off only as a baseline. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether radios sense the channel before choosing a resource. `false` is the random selection baseline (Ali et al. 2021 §II.1). Unset is on. Whether radios listen before booking a slot. Off is the random-selection baseline. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-candidate-percent"></span>`radio.sidelink.candidate_percent` | integer | % | | [20, 50]<br>recommended 20 % (LTE's fixed value); 35 or 50 % on NR. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of the selection window that must survive exclusion before a radio picks: 20 % (LTE's fixed value), 35 % or 50 % (NR only). Unset is 20 %. The share of resources that must remain after exclusion before a radio picks one. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-selection-window-ms"></span>`radio.sidelink.selection_window_ms` | integer | ms | | [1, 100]<br>recommended 100 ms at 10 Hz; at most the message interval. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How late after a message is ready its new resource may be (the selection window's end T2), ms. Shorter cuts latency but leaves fewer resources to pick from; at most the message interval. Unset is the profile's (100 ms at 10 Hz). How late after a message is ready its new resource may be. Shorter cuts latency but leaves fewer resources to pick from. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-noise-figure-db"></span>`radio.sidelink.noise_figure_db` | number | dB | | [0, 15]<br>recommended 9 dB (3GPP TR 36.885 UE); 6 dB for a good automotive module. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The UE receiver noise figure, dB: TR 36.885 Annex A.1.1's 9 dB unless set. It moves every sidelink noise floor (and the candidate range measured against it). How much noise a C-V2X receiver's own electronics add; every extra dB shortens the range at which a transport block still decodes. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-cbr-threshold-dbm"></span>`radio.sidelink.cbr_threshold_dbm` | number | dBm | | [-112, -8]<br>recommended -94 dBm (this build's default); -112 to -80 dBm in 2 dB steps (TS 36.331). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `sl-ThresS-RSSI-CBR`, dBm: the S-RSSI above which a sub-channel counts as busy in the channel busy ratio (TS 36.214 §5.1.30, TS 36.331 range -112 to -8 dBm in 2 dB steps). -94 dBm unless set; the CR limits and every CBR metric read it. The signal level above which a C-V2X sub-channel counts as busy in the channel busy ratio, which drives congestion control. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-align-generation"></span>`radio.sidelink.align_generation` | boolean | | | recommended Off (today's default, every LTE-V2X run unchanged); on for a deployment-faithful LTE-V2X latency. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Whether each radio generates its periodic BSM just before its reserved resource, as SAE J3161/1 has the application do, instead of on its own 100 ms clock: the BSM then waits a margin for its resource rather than up to a whole period. The phase follows every reselection; an interval it changes stays inside J2945/1's bounds. Unset is off. Whether each C-V2X radio builds its safety message just before its reserved slot, as SAE J3161/1 has deployed radios do, so the message waits a millisecond or two for the air instead of up to a tenth of a second. |
| <span id="s-radio-sidelink-align-margin-ms"></span>`radio.sidelink.align_margin_ms` | number | ms | | [0, 50]<br>recommended 1 ms (the radio's processing time T1); an assumption until J3161/1's own figure is read. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How long before its reserved resource an aligned BSM reaches the radio, ms, on top of the device's longest signing time. Unset is the pool's processing time `T1` (1 ms on LTE-V2X): an ASSUMPTION until J3161/1's figure is read. With aligned generation, how long before its reserved slot the signed message reaches the radio, on top of the longest time the device takes to sign it. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`radio.rat`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `dsrc-80211p` | DSRC / ITS-G5 (IEEE 802.11p) | Wi-Fi-based V2X: listen-before-talk on a 10 MHz channel. The US pilots' radio and Europe's ITS-G5. |
 | `lte-v2x-pc5` | C-V2X, LTE sidelink (PC5 Mode 4) | 3GPP Release 14 cellular V2X without a network: sensing-based semi-persistent scheduling on the SAE J3161/1 profile. |
 | `nr-v2x-pc5` | C-V2X, 5G NR sidelink (PC5 Mode 2) | 3GPP Release 16 sidelink at 30 kHz on the ETSI EN 303 798 pool. No US deployment profile exists yet. |
 | `hybrid` | Hybrid (not available) | Refused by this build: the hybrid selector arbitrates a direct radio against cellular, which is not wired. |

??? note "`radio.region`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `us` | United States, 2024 rules (FCC 24-123) | C-V2X only on 5.905-5.925 GHz; DSRC is refused because its licences end in December 2026. |
 | `us-2016` | United States, DSRC band plan (2016) | 802.11p on channel 172, the plan SAE J2945/1 was written for (47 CFR 90.377). |
 | `eu` | Europe (ETSI EN 302 571) | 10 MHz channels at up to 33 dBm EIRP; ITS-G5, LTE-V2X and NR-V2X side by side. |

 | Value | Label | Meaning |

 | `172` | Channel 172 (5.860 GHz, 10 MHz) | us-2016: Service channel for safety of life and property: the J2945/1 BSM channel; eu: ITS-G5B, non-safety ITS |
 | `174` | Channel 174 (5.870 GHz, 10 MHz) | us-2016: Service channel; eu: ITS-G5B, non-safety ITS |
 | `176` | Channel 176 (5.880 GHz, 10 MHz) | us-2016: Service channel; eu: ITS-G5A road safety (SCH1); 5GAA's 5G-V2X block |
 | `178` | Channel 178 (5.890 GHz, 10 MHz) | us-2016: Control channel (44.8 dBm for state or local government); eu: ITS-G5A road safety (SCH2); 5GAA's 5G-V2X block |
 | `180` | Channel 180 (5.900 GHz, 10 MHz) | us: C-V2X 10 MHz; 23 dBm for an OBU without geofencing (federal radar); us-2016: Service channel; eu: ITS-G5A road safety, the control channel where ITS-G5 deploys |
 | `181` | Channel 181 (5.905 GHz, 20 MHz) | us: C-V2X 20 MHz including 5.895-5.905 GHz |
 | `182` | Channel 182 (5.910 GHz, 10 MHz) | us: C-V2X 10 MHz; us-2016: Service channel; eu: Road safety ITS; the LTE-V2X day-1 channel 5GAA proposed |
 | `183` | Channel 183 (5.915 GHz, 20 MHz) | us: C-V2X 20 MHz: the SAE J3161/1 LTE-V2X deployment channel |
 | `184` | Channel 184 (5.920 GHz, 10 MHz) | us: C-V2X 10 MHz; us-2016: Public safety, safety of life and property (40 dBm for public safety) |

??? note "`radio.tiers.propagation`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Simplified (abstract) — free space, no buildings | Free-space loss with no buildings, shadowing or fading: each link is cheaper to price, but with nothing in the way more links reach each receiver, so a city run costs about as much as Standard; cap radio.range.max_m to make a large fleet cheap. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) | Frame-level or geometry-traced detail: the most faithful and the slowest. |

??? note "`radio.tiers.phy`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Fast (abstract) — runs as Standard | This build has no separate abstract PHY: the Standard (medium) reception model runs. Only propagation and channel access have an abstract tier. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) | Frame-level or geometry-traced detail: the most faithful and the slowest. |

??? note "`radio.tiers.mac`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Simplified (abstract) — no channel access | Every frame goes on air when it is queued, with no carrier sense, backoff or channel busy ratio (so no congestion control); it saves little run time, because receptions, not channel access, are most of the cost. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) — runs as Standard | Channel access has no separate high tier in this build: the Standard EDCA model runs. Choosing it is what allows the Detailed physical layer. |

??? note "`radio.tiers.focus.tier`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `abstract` | Fast (abstract) — not possible here | A focus region exists to run higher than the world around it, and no tier is below abstract; choose Standard or Detailed. |
 | `medium` | Standard (medium) | The models the literature agrees on, without frame-level detail. The usual choice. |
 | `high` | Detailed (high) | Frame-level or geometry-traced detail: the most faithful and the slowest. |

??? note "`radio.devices.obu.antenna_pattern`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `tr37885` | By vehicle type (3GPP TR 37.885) | A roof antenna on cars and vans, front and rear panels on trucks and buses. The default. |
 | `rooftop` | Roof antenna on every vehicle | The same all-round roof antenna on every vehicle, trucks included. |
 | `isotropic` | No pattern (isotropic) | The same gain in every direction: the textbook simplification. |

??? note "`radio.devices.obu.sampled_pattern.rotation_jitter`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | None | Every mount at `rotation_deg`. |
 | `uniform` | Uniform | Uniform in ±`rotation_jitter_deg` per vehicle. |
 | `normal` | Normal | Normal with σ = `rotation_jitter_deg` per vehicle. |

??? note "`radio.adjacent_channel[].rat`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `dsrc-80211p` | DSRC / ITS-G5 (IEEE 802.11p) | Wi-Fi-based V2X: listen-before-talk on a 10 MHz channel. The US pilots' radio and Europe's ITS-G5. |
 | `lte-v2x-pc5` | C-V2X, LTE sidelink (PC5 Mode 4) | 3GPP Release 14 cellular V2X without a network: sensing-based semi-persistent scheduling on the SAE J3161/1 profile. |
 | `nr-v2x-pc5` | C-V2X, 5G NR sidelink (PC5 Mode 2) | 3GPP Release 16 sidelink at 30 kHz on the ETSI EN 303 798 pool. No US deployment profile exists yet. |
 | `hybrid` | Hybrid (not available) | Refused by this build: the hybrid selector arbitrates a direct radio against cellular, which is not wired. |

??? note "`radio.mac.edca_profile`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `by-region` | By region | SAE J2945/1 Table 18 for 802.11p under a US region, ETSI EN 302 663 everywhere else. |
 | `sae-j2945-1` | SAE J2945/1 Table 18 (BSM at AC_VI, critical BSM at AC_VO) | AC_VI CWmin 15, CWmax 1023, AIFSN 4 (UPEDCA-003); a BSM without a critical event flag waits at user priority 5, one with a flag at 7. |
 | `en-302-663` | ETSI EN 302 663 (OCB defaults) | The 802.11 OCB defaults: AC_VI CWmin 7, CWmax 15, AIFSN 3. |

??? note "`radio.mac.periodic_access_category`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `vo` | Voice (AC_VO, highest) | The shortest wait (AIFSN 2, CWmin 3): where SAE J2945/1 puts a BSM with a critical event flag (user priority 7) and EN 302 663 the DENM. |
 | `vi` | Video (AC_VI) (SAE J2945/1 UP 5) | Where SAE J2945/1 puts a BSM without a critical event flag (user priority 5, UPEDCA-001) and EN 302 663 Annex C the CAM: AIFSN 4, CWmin 15 under J2945/1 Table 18; AIFSN 3, CWmin 7 under EN 302 663. |
 | `be` | Best effort (AC_BE) | AIFSN 6, CWmin 15: ordinary data, yields to every safety message. |
 | `bk` | Background (AC_BK, lowest) | AIFSN 9, CWmin 15: the longest wait. |

??? note "`radio.mac.event_access_category`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `vo` | Voice (AC_VO, highest) | The shortest wait (AIFSN 2, CWmin 3): where SAE J2945/1 puts a BSM with a critical event flag (user priority 7) and EN 302 663 the DENM. |
 | `vi` | Video (AC_VI) | AIFSN 4, CWmin 15 under SAE J2945/1 Table 18; AIFSN 3, CWmin 7 under EN 302 663. |
 | `be` | Best effort (AC_BE) | AIFSN 6, CWmin 15: ordinary data, yields to every safety message. |
 | `bk` | Background (AC_BK, lowest) | AIFSN 9, CWmin 15: the longest wait. |

??? note "`radio.channel_model.fading`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `none` | None | No small-scale fading: the received power is the path loss and shadowing only. |
 | `rayleigh` | Rayleigh | No direct path, only scattered copies: the harshest common fading (Nakagami m = 1). |
 | `rice` | Rice | A direct path plus scatter; its strength over the scatter is the Rice factor K. |
 | `nakagami` | Nakagami-m | The V2V literature's usual fit; its shape m runs from 1 (Rayleigh) up to milder channels. |

??? note "`radio.channel_model.fading_coherence`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `independent` | Independent per message | Every message on a link gets its own fade, whatever the speeds. |
 | `doppler` | Doppler (speed-dependent) | A fade lasts one coherence time: long for vehicles standing still, a fraction of a millisecond at highway speed. |

??? note "`radio.dcc.reactive_table`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `a1` | Table A.1 (frames up to 1 ms) | 10 Hz relaxed down to 1 Hz restrictive (TS 102 687 V1.2.1 Table A.1). The default. |
 | `a2` | Table A.2 (frames up to 500 µs) | 20 Hz relaxed down to 1 Hz restrictive, for short frames (Table A.2). |

??? note "`radio.dcc.channel_quality`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sae-j2945-1` | SAE J2945/1 Eq. 4 (capped mean PER) | The mean loss rate of the neighbours within 100 m over 5 s, capped at 0.3, recomputed every second. The default. |
 | `fmvss150-nprm` | FMVSS 150 NPRM (0.9 smoothing) | The same mean, smoothed with weight 0.9 on the previous value as the withdrawn 2017 NPRM transcribed it: reacts about ten times slower. |
